mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in a 3-month window
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-rate periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by monthly PAYEMS exceeds 2% for two consecutive months signals labor market strength that supports corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth > 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no correlation with PAYEMS momentum (Pearson's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) by more than 5% in a month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which typically precedes a decline in equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during confirmed demand contractions (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of over 10% over three months suggests supply-side constraints that raise uncertainty and discount future cash flows, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain positive despite INDPRO declines (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% while UNRATE remains below 6%, it indicates a shift from contractionary to neutral policy, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically positive during confirmed policy normalization (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) exceeding 5% suggests a cooling labor market, which often precedes a negative shock to equities and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by > 0.5% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months and crosses above 5%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no significant negative relationship with UNRATE changes (R-squared < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both HOUST (retail sales) and RSAFS (federal reserve balance sheet) by at least 3% in the same quarter indicates dual demand and liquidity pressures, which are associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative during such dual pressures (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where industrial production (INDPRO) remains below its 50th percentile for three consecutive months, the uncertainty about supply availability tends to raise required rates of return, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with INDPRO deviations from trend (Spearman's rho > 0.2).
